group.passage:
A windmill is a device for tapping the energy of the wind by means of sails mounted on a rotating shaft. Like waterwheels, windmills were among the original prime movers that replaced humans as a source of power. The most important use of the windmill was for grinding grain between stones. In certain areas its uses in land drainage and water pumping were equally important.
The first windmill originated in Persia around the 9th century. With sails radiating from a vertical shaft standing in a fixed building, this vertical-axis windmill, derived from the earliest water mills, was used to drive a single pair of stones directly, without the use of gears. Persian millwrights, taken prisoner by the forces of Genghis Khan, were sent to China to instruct in the building of windmills; their use for irrigation there has lasted ever since.
In the 12th century, the first horizontal-axis windmill, called the post mill, appeared in Europe. It was developed directly from the Roman water mill with its right-angle drive to the stones through a single pair of gears attached to the shaft that holds the sails on the other end. The post mill features a boxlike body, which contains the gearing, millstones, and machinery and carries the sails, well balanced on a wooden post supported by quarterbars. The body can be turned so that the sails can be faced into the wind.
More advanced smock and tower mills were made in the following centuries. The smock mill consists of a sloping thatched wooden tower for holding the milling machinery. It is topped with a rotatable cap, which holds just the roof, the sails and the shaft. It differs from a post mill in that the body does not rotate; it is the cap that rotates to face the wind. Therefore, the body can be made much taller, which can house more pairs of stones and allow the sails to catch more wind. The tower mill takes the smock mill design even further, by replacing the wooden body with a brick or stone built tower. This makes the tower mill more weatherproof and fireproof.
The rapid decline in the use of windmills began following World War I with the development of the internal-combustion engine and the spread of electric power.

figures.label: 第4題選項圖片 (A)–(D)
figures.caption: 第4題：四張風車的黑白照片
figures.description: 第4題的四個選項都是黑白照片，排成兩列兩欄。(A)（左上，橫幅）：天空下一排厚實的土牆（泥磚）建築，牆頂上豎立著一整排高大的木架，木架內是許多直立排列的木條格柵，像一面面直立的牆板，沒有向外伸出的十字形翼板；土牆下方開有幾個小門與階梯。(B)（右上，直幅）：空曠草地上一座木造風車：一個方盒狀（箱形）的風車身架在一根中央木柱上，木柱底部由數根斜向伸出的木條支撐在地面上；風車身一側裝著格狀的翼板，整個風車身懸空、看起來可以繞著木柱轉動。(C)（左下，直幅）：一座下寬上窄、多邊形的高塔式風車，塔身表面有橫向條紋（看似木板）、開有數扇小窗，塔頂是一個帽狀頂蓋，頂蓋前方伸出很長的翼板，後方裝有一個小型的扇狀風輪（扇尾）。(D)（右下，直幅）：一座高大、下寬上窄的深色圓塔風車，塔身看起來由磚石砌成，塔頂有淺色的帽狀頂蓋，裝有四片格狀翼板與小型扇尾，塔下周圍有樹木與房屋。

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT a common use for windmills?
Based on the passage, what is the key difference between a vertical-axis windmill and a horizontal-axis windmill?

options.A: The former uses more sails than the latter.
options.B: The former is built with wood while the latter is made of bricks.
options.C: The former takes up less room than the latter.
options.D: The former operates without gears, but the latter requires gears to drive the millstones.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The first windmill was credited to Genghis Khan.
options.B: The destruction of World War I caused a sharp drop in the use of windmills.
options.C: With a fixed, taller body, the smock mill works more efficiently than the post mill.
options.D: Persian millwrights taught Europeans how to build horizontal-axis windmills.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following pictures best represents the image of a typical post mill?

options.A: ［圖］土牆建築頂上豎立一整排直立木條格柵的木架，沒有向外伸出的十字形翼板
options.B: ［圖］草地上一個箱形木造風車身架在一根中央木柱上，柱底由數根斜撐木條支撐，風車身一側裝有格狀翼板
options.C: ［圖］下寬上窄、開有小窗的多邊形高塔（塔身表面有橫向條紋），塔頂帽狀頂蓋前裝長翼板、後有小扇尾
options.D: ［圖］高大、下寬上窄的深色圓塔（看似磚石砌成），塔頂淺色帽狀頂蓋上裝四片格狀翼板與小扇尾，周圍有樹木與房屋
